claims.text: A partitioned table is a virtual table with no storage of its own; every row inserted through it is routed to the partition whose bounds match the partition key value. Queries and inserts may name the parent table.
In a range partition FOR VALUES FROM (a) TO (b), the lower bound is inclusive and the upper bound exclusive, so 2026-03-01 00:00+07 belongs to orders_2026_03.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.12.2 Declarative Partitioning (range bounds); SQL command CREATE TABLE (PARTITION OF, FOR VALUES)

claims.text: Partition pruning: with a WHERE condition on the partition key compared to constants, the planner excludes partitions whose bounds show they cannot hold matching rows (enable_partition_pruning is on by default).
Without a condition on the partition key, no partition can be pruned and the plan reads every partition, combining them under an Append node.

A unique constraint bars two rows sharing a value in its columns. On a partitioned table it, like a primary key, must include all partition key columns, as each partition's index checks only its partition; error: 'unique constraint on partitioned table must include all partitioning columns'.

Old data can be removed by dropping its partition directly, or by ALTER TABLE ... DETACH PARTITION first (the partition becomes a standalone table that can be kept or dropped); either avoids the row-by-row work (and VACUUM overhead) of a bulk DELETE.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.12.1 Overview (bulk loads and deletes), 5.12.2.2 Partition Maintenance; SQL command ALTER TABLE (DETACH PARTITION)

claims.text: Every partition of orders_by_month is created with CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF, so it is an ordinary table in the same database on the same PostgreSQL server and shares that server's CPU, memory and disk.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.12.2 Declarative Partitioning (partitions are ordinary tables); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 db/partitioning/orders-by-month.sql

claims.text: CREATE INDEX on a partitioned table creates a matching index on each partition (here orders_2026_0N_customer_id_idx); orders-by-month.sql line 33 creates it on orders_by_month.

claims.text: The partition key is usually chosen from the queries the table answers most: when most queries filter by month, a monthly range key on placed_at lets them be pruned.
